'''''Visnaga daucoides''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[Apiaceae|carrot family]] known by many common names, including '''toothpick-plant''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''toothpickweed''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=AMVI2|taxon=Ammi visnaga|accessdate=8 January 2016}}</ref> '''bisnaga''', '''khella''', or sometimes [[bishop's weed]]. It is native to Europe, Asia, and North Africa, but it can be found throughout the world as an [[introduced species]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Visnaga daucoides Gaertn. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:849956-1 |access-date=2022-07-06 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref> 

==Description==
This is an erect [[annual plant]] growing from a [[taproot]] to a maximum height near {{Convert|80|cm|in|sp=us}}. The leaves are up to {{Convert|20|cm|in|sp=us}} long and generally oval to triangular in shape but dissected into many small linear to lance-shaped segments. The [[inflorescence]] is a compound [[umbel]] of white flowers similar to those of other Apiaceae species. The fruit is a compressed oval-shaped body less than 3 millimeters long. This  species is a source of [[khellin]], a [[diuretic]] extract.

Like its close relative ''[[Ammi majus]]'', ''Visnaga daucoides'' is commonly seen in gardens where it is grown from seed annually.<ref>{{cite web
| url = http://higgledygarden.com/2015/01/07/growing-ammi-visnaga-and-ammi-majus-from-seed/
| title = Growing ''Ammi visnaga'' and ''Ammi majus'' from seed
| publisher = higgledygarden.com
| access-date = 12 January 2018
| date = 2015-01-07
| archive-date = 2018-01-13
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180113042449/http://higgledygarden.com/2015/01/07/growing-ammi-visnaga-and-ammi-majus-from-seed/

}}</ref>

Some authorities regard ''Visnaga daucoides'' as a [[synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] of '''''Ammi visnaga'''''; and it is still widely referenced under that name.<ref name = GRIN>{{GRIN}}</ref>
 
==Traditional medicine==
In Egypt, a [[tea]] made from the fruit of this species has been used as a [[herbal remedy]] for [[kidney stones]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Azim Khan|first1=Muhammad|title=Phytochemistry and Medicinal Properties of Ammi Visnaga|journal=Pak. J. Bot.|date=2014|volume=46|issue=3|pages=861–867}}</ref>

Preparations of the fruits have also been used for [[angina pectoris]] therapy.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Waltenberger | first1 = B | last2 = Mocan | first2 = A | last3 = Šmejkal | first3 = K | last4 = Heiss | first4 = EH | last5 = Atanasov | first5 = AG | year = 2016| title = Natural Products to Counteract the Epidemic of Cardiovascular and Metabolic Disorders | journal = Molecules | volume = 55 | issue = 6| page = 555 | doi = 10.3390/molecules21060807 | pmid = 27338339 | pmc = 4928700 | doi-access = free }}</ref>

==Laboratory research==
Laboratory rat studies show that the extract slows the buildup of [[calcium oxalate]] crystals in the kidneys and acts as a [[diuretic]].<ref name=vana>{{cite journal | last1 = Vanachayangkul | first1 = P. | display-authors = etal | year = 2010 | title = An aqueous extract of ''Ammi visnaga'' fruits and its constituents khellin and visnagin prevent cell damage caused by oxalate in renal epithelial cells | journal = Phytomedicine | volume = 17 | issue = 8| pages = 653–58 | pmc = 3618668 | pmid = 20036111 | doi = 10.1016/j.phymed.2009.10.011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Khan | first1 = Z. A. | display-authors = etal | year = 2001 | title = Inhibition of oxalate nephrolithiasis with ''Ammi visnaga'' (AI-Khillah) | journal = International Urology and Nephrology | volume = 33 | issue = 4| pages = 605–8 | doi = 10.1023/A:1020526517097 | pmid = 12452606 | s2cid = 12832121 }}</ref> Its clinical effects in humans are unknown.

==Chemical constituents==
[[Khellin]], a [[chemical compound]] obtained from ''Visnaga daucoides'', was used at one time as a [[smooth muscle relaxant]], but its use is now limited due to adverse [[side effects]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Ziment | first1 = I | year = 1998 | title = How your patients may be using herbalism to treat their asthma - Herbal products are becoming increasingly popular for treating a variety of medical complaints - including asthma. What are these | journal = Journal of Respiratory Diseases | volume = 19 | issue = 12| pages = 1070–83 }}</ref> [[Amiodarone]] and [[cromoglycate]] are synthetic [[derivative (chemistry)|derivatives]] of khellin with fewer side effects which were developed for use in modern medicine.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hollman |first1=A |title=Plants in Cardiology: Amiodarone, nifedipine, sodium cromoglycate |journal=British Heart Journal |date=1991 |volume=65 |page=57 |doi=10.1136/hrt.65.1.57|pmc=1024467 }}</ref>

[[Visnagin]] is another chemical compound found in ''Visnaga daucoides'', which is toxic if ingested in the pure state.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Lee | first1 = J. K. | display-authors = etal | title = Anti-inflammatory effect of visnagin in lipopolysaccharide-stimulated BV-2 microglial cells | journal = Archives of Pharmacal Research | volume = 33 | issue = 11| pages = 1843–50 | pmid = 21116788 | doi = 10.1007/s12272-010-1117-1 | date = November 2010 | s2cid = 22168754 }}</ref> [[Visnadine]] is a natural [[vasodilator]] found in ''Visnaga daucoides.''
